title: Increasing the Accessibility and Applicability of Active Inference: Generative Playbooks and Open-Source Summer School Curriculum Development
description: This letter was submitted to the Dana Frontiers program in January 2025, on behalf of the Active Inference Institute , in pursuit of funding several promising activities (generative playbooks for applying Active Inference, and a Summer School program). Though this application was not funded, we have uploaded it as an open source artefact here, seeking participation and resourcing for these and other projects, in due time, place, and fashion.

methods.name: Proposed stipended community working groups to co-create playbooks
methods.description: The letter proposes Institute officers coordinating weekly working groups of paid community members to co-create Active Inference playbooks for target audiences.
methods.evidence: Officers of the Institute will coordinate the co-creation of playbooks with members of our community through working groups. Contributing members will receive a stipend for their participation.

methods.name: Planned use of generative AI for multi-language, multi-level materials
methods.description: Generative AI is proposed to make playbook materials available across languages, media, and levels of technical detail.
methods.evidence: Appropriate usage of generative AI to ensure materials are available in different languages, media, and levels of technical detail.

methods.name: Planned multi-perspective Summer School curriculum design
methods.description: A Summer School course is proposed that teaches Active Inference principles from sociology, philosophy, mathematics and linguistics perspectives.
methods.evidence: we will design a course that teaches principles of Active Inference from multiple perspectives, including sociology, philosophy, mathematics and linguistics.

methods.name: Planned evaluation via advisory board review, interviews, and surveys
methods.description: Progress is to be evaluated through quarterly internal feedback, interviews with target groups, and surveys of Summer School participants.
methods.evidence: The playbook will have internal quarterly feedback as we develop it, with further interviews with the target groups who apply the

key_findings: The letter commits to producing playbooks for Active Inference adoption targeted at neuroscience graduate students, educators and policy-makers.
It commits to an open-source Summer School curriculum in Active Inference, supporting an in-person 2025 event and versioned over subsequent years.
The Summer School template is to be published openly so that groups worldwide can run their own courses.
The proposed budget totals $100,000, split between personnel for the two initiatives and computing resources.
key_findings_evidence: Playbooks for Active inference adoption targeted to key populations (neuroscience graduate students, educators and policy-makers).
A Summer School curriculum (open-source) in Active Inference for diverse backgrounds, in support of an in-person event to be held in 2025 & versioned over the coming years.
the template for a Summer School will be available publicly on our website, so that groups across the world can start their own summer course
$45,000 for personnel for the Summer School curriculum initiative.
